starting_workspace.sources/01-architecture.md:
# Execution architecture

Current supported execution surfaces are **local workstation** and **GitHub Actions**. A remote VM runner is not currently a supported Series 1 surface. Local runs obtain provider credentials from the process environment. GitHub runs obtain the same provider credential from an Actions secret.
starting_workspace.sources/02-meeting-2026-07-12.md:
# Meeting note — 2026-07-12

We may add a remote VM runner later if repeated experiments need a long-lived host. This was discussed as a possible future extension; no acceptance or implementation decision was made.
starting_workspace.sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md:
# Validation log — 2026-08-01

The harness was exercised successfully on a local workstation and on a clean GitHub-hosted runner. The remote VM path has not been tested. Functional records match structurally across the two validated surfaces. We have not yet established whether GitHub-hosted runner variance materially distorts latency comparisons against local runs.

history.content:
Research note (sources only; workspace unedited, no outside knowledge used)

(1) Currently supported execution surfaces — two: the local workstation and GitHub Actions. A remote VM runner is expressly not a supported Series 1 surface at present [sources/01-architecture.md].

(2) Evidence establishing this — two independent supports: (a) the architecture note declares local and GitHub Actions as the supported surfaces and specifies credential handling (process environment locally; an Actions secret on GitHub) [sources/01-architecture.md]; (b) the validation log records the harness exercised successfully on both — a local workstation and a clean GitHub-hosted runner — with functional records matching structurally across the two [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md]. The remote VM path has not been tested [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md], consistent with its exclusion [sources/01-architecture.md].

(3) Superseded statement — the early-plan assumption that Series 1 would run locally only because CI could not carry the required model configuration [sources/99-archive-early-plan.md]. That file predates the Actions dispatcher and is retained only as planning history; since GitHub Actions is now a supported, validated surface, the local-only assumption no longer holds.

(4) Unresolved on comparing runs — it is not yet established whether GitHub-hosted runner variance materially distorts latency comparisons against local runs [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md]. Structural equivalence of functional records is confirmed, but cross-surface latency comparison remains unvalidated. Relatedly, a remote VM runner exists only as a discussed possible future extension with no acceptance or implementation decision [sources/02-meeting-2026-07-12.md], so no third surface can enter any comparison today.

capabilities.name: situate

capabilities.name: close
capabilities.description: The return condition: when the bounded request is realised, close the work at determination (P5); what passes reads as the return (P5'). Args: {"synthesis": string} — what is actually realised, in plain text. The workspace checks run on close.

capabilities.name: lens_reading
capabilities.description: A lens reading of a subject you name: how that subject reads through twelve lenses right now, returned as a distribution with the strongest lens named. The reading is taken fresh on each call; it is a reading of the subject, never an identity assigned to it. Args: {"subject": string} — name the subject concretely (the task, a decision, a file, the work as it stands).

result.content:
Research note (sources only; workspace unedited, no outside knowledge used)

(1) Currently supported execution surfaces — two: the local workstation and GitHub Actions. A remote VM runner is expressly not a supported Series 1 surface at present [sources/01-architecture.md].

(2) Evidence establishing this — two independent supports: (a) the architecture note declares local and GitHub Actions as the supported surfaces and specifies credential handling (process environment locally; an Actions secret on GitHub) [sources/01-architecture.md]; (b) the validation log records the harness exercised successfully on both — a local workstation and a clean GitHub-hosted runner — with functional records matching structurally across the two [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md]. The remote VM path has not been tested [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md], consistent with its exclusion [sources/01-architecture.md].

(3) Superseded statement — the early-plan assumption that Series 1 would run locally only because CI could not carry the required model configuration [sources/99-archive-early-plan.md]. That file predates the Actions dispatcher and is retained only as planning history; since GitHub Actions is now a supported, validated surface, the local-only assumption no longer holds.

(4) Unresolved on comparing runs — it is not yet established whether GitHub-hosted runner variance materially distorts latency comparisons against local runs [sources/03-validation-2026-08-01.md]. Structural equivalence of functional records is confirmed, but cross-surface latency comparison remains unvalidated. Relatedly, a remote VM runner exists only as a discussed possible future extension with no acceptance or implementation decision [sources/02-meeting-2026-07-12.md], so no third surface can enter any comparison today.

Every material claim is cited to a filename. No workspace edits; no outside knowledge.
